Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-\int (-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+{\frac{1}{5}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{5}\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)]+[\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =[-\frac{\pi }{25}\cdot (-1)+0]+[0-0] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)]+[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}-0]+[0-1] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{3x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}

$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}2x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{2}{3}x{e}^{3x}|}_{0}^{1/3}-\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}{e}^{3x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{2}{3}x{e}^{3x}|}_{0}^{1/3}-{\frac{2}{9}{e}^{3x}|}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3(1/3)}-0\cdot {e}^{3\cdot 0}]-\frac{2}{9}[{e}^{3(1/3)}-{e}^{3\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\frac{e}{3}-0]-\frac{2}{9}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{2e}{9}-\frac{2e}{9}+\frac{2}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}-{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x){|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})]+\frac{1}{4}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4}]+\frac{1}{4}[0-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[0]+0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & +[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 0-\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}]+[1-\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi }{12}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}(x{e}^{2x}){|}_{0}^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(x{e}^{2x}){|}_{0}^{1/2}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{4}{|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2(1/2)}-0\cdot {e}^{2\cdot 0}]-\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{2(1/2)}-{e}^{2\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{e}{2}-0]-\frac{1}{4}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{e}{4}-\frac{e-1}{4} \\  & =\frac{e-e+1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}-{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2} \\  & =2[\frac{3\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & +2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =2[-\frac{3\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2}]+2[0-0] \\  & =2(-2\pi )+0 \\  & =-4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4}-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}{e}^{4x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4}-{\frac{1}{16}{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4(1/4)}-0\cdot {e}^{4\cdot 0}]-\frac{1}{16}[{e}^{4(1/4)}-{e}^{4\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{e}{4}-0]-\frac{1}{16}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{e}{16}-\frac{e}{16}+\frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=12x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=12 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 12x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =12x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 12\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }12x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-12x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }+12{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-12x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }+12\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =-12[\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi )] \\  & +12[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )] \\  & =-12[-\pi -\pi ]+12[0-0] \\  & =-12[-2\pi ] \\  & =24\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+4(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 1-0\cdot 0)+4(0-1) \\  & =2\pi -4.\end{aligned}
$$
